metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Smithton, PA
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Smithton, PA along the Youghiogheny? We buy Westmoreland County Marcellus interests directly, cash offers, no pressure.
heroLead: Smithton sits right on the Youghiogheny, one of the small river towns in Westmoreland County where a family's mineral rights are usually worth more than anyone in the house realizes until someone actually checks.
intro: Smithton is a small borough on the Youghiogheny River in Westmoreland County, close to the Fayette County line, in a stretch of the wet-gas Marcellus window that's seen steady operator interest for over a decade. Range Resources and CNX have both worked this general area, and unit development has, over the years, reached parcels along both sides of the river.

A lot of Smithton-area mineral interests are tied to riverfront or hillside tracts that have been in the same family for generations, sometimes with a lease signed back during the initial 2008 to 2010 boom that nobody has looked at closely since.

sections.heading: Old Leases That Never Got a Second Look
paragraphs: If your family signed a lease near Smithton fifteen or more years ago, it's worth pulling that document out and actually reading the post-production cost language now, especially if you've noticed your royalty checks running smaller than gas price headlines would suggest. Under Kilmer v. Elexco, Pennsylvania courts have generally allowed operators to deduct gathering and compression costs when the lease permits it, and a lot of older leases do.

sections.heading: What Your Interest Is Actually Worth
paragraphs: We look at whether your tract sits inside an active unit, review production history where available, and check current DEP permits for anything planned nearby. From there we give you a cash offer built on real numbers, not a guess based on what a neighbor's cousin got a decade ago.

faqs.question: How do I check whether my old Smithton-area lease is still in force?
faqs.answer: Look at the habendum clause and compare it against whether a well within your unit has continued producing. Most standard leases stay in force as long as the unit is held by production.

faqs.question: Why does my royalty check seem smaller than expected?
faqs.answer: Post-production deductions for gathering, compression, and transportation are the most common cause. We can review your specific lease language to explain exactly what's being deducted.

faqs.question: Do you buy interests along the river even if access is limited?
faqs.answer: Yes, surface access has no bearing on mineral rights value. We evaluate based on your unit and production, not surface conditions.

faqs.question: What if I've never actually seen my lease document?
faqs.answer: That happens more often than you'd think, especially when the lease was signed by a parent or grandparent. We can help locate a recorded copy at the Westmoreland County recorder of deeds if your own copy has been lost.
